title: From Post-Pregnancy Arthritis to CWG Bronze: Seema Kaliramna Eyes Asian Games Medal
excerpt: The 27-year-old discus thrower from Haryana returned from severe arthritis after childbirth to win Commonwealth Games bronze, and now targets the Asian Games in Japan as a step toward the Olympics.
body:
• Seema Kaliramna, 27, won a bronze medal in discus throw at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow with a 58.65m throw
  • She returned to competition after suffering severe arthritis following the birth of her son in 2022, when she could barely walk 10 meters
  • Her personal best of 59.73m this season has her targeting a medal at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, starting September 19
  • Coached by her husband Ravinder, and supported by the Inspire Institute of Sport, she views the Asian Games as the next step toward her Olympic dream

Three years ago, Seema Kaliramna could not walk 10 meters. On September 19, she will step into the discus circle at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, carrying a Commonwealth Games bronze medal and a personal best of 59.73 meters.

The 27-year-old from Bhiwani, Haryana, has emerged as one of Indian athletics' most compelling comeback stories. After severe arthritis following childbirth threatened to end her career, Kaliramna has not merely returned — she has thrown further than she ever did before motherhood.

The Road Back From Arthritis

Kaliramna married her coach, Ravinder 'Monu' Kaliramna, in 2019. She was preparing for the World University Games at the time, throwing 54–55 meters in training. A knee injury and then COVID-19 kept her away from competition. Then came pregnancy.

https://x.com/gulf_news/status/2097183510301659456

Her son Rudra was born in 2022. The period around childbirth left Kaliramna dealing with frozen shoulder and hip, conditions that worsened after delivery. Doctors diagnosed severe arthritis.

"At that time, I was not able to walk up to 10 meters, and I was not able to pick up my child."

— Seema Kaliramna

At her lowest, she questioned whether continuing was possible. Her husband's response was to restart her training gradually, building muscle at a pace her body could handle and avoiding steroids. As the muscle developed, the arthritis eased.

Kaliramna returned to competition in 2024. Her best competition throw before motherhood had been 48.08 meters. Within a year of returning, she hit 57.19 meters. She won the 2025 National Games. This season, she has gone beyond 59 meters.

CWG Bronze and Rising Confidence

At the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Kaliramna secured bronze with a throw of 58.65 meters, behind Jamaica's Samantha Hall (61.66m) and Canada's Julia Tunks (60.67m). She started with a foul, bounced back with 57.32 meters, and delivered her medal-winning throw in the third round.

The bronze carried added weight. At the 2025 Asian Championships, she had returned empty-handed — a result she described as deeply disappointing. "The experience I gained then helped me achieve this result," she told ANI after winning in Glasgow.

Since the CWG, Kaliramna competed at the World Athletics Silver Level Continental Tour in Bhubaneswar on August 22, finishing fourth with 57.44 meters against a field that included Commonwealth champion Hall. She was characteristically measured about the result: "It is not that bad. According to the Asian Games, it is good."

A PhD Scholar With Olympic Ambitions

Beyond the throwing circle, Kaliramna is pursuing a doctoral degree with a thesis titled "Impact of Imaginary and Positive Self-Talk Training on Athletes' Performance." She applied those mental techniques during the CWG, using positive self-talk to refocus after her opening foul.

Neither Kaliramna nor her husband hold government or private jobs. Their training has been supported by the Inspire Institute of Sport, which has provided physiotherapy, massage, travel, and accommodation for the past year and a half. At a Haryana government event in Panchkula on August 26, she was approached about a junior coach position — but for now, the discus remains the priority.

What's Next: Asian Games and Beyond

The 2026 Asian Games run from September 19 to October 4. Kaliramna has already cleared the qualifying mark of 55.48 meters. She is not setting a target distance.

"I just want to throw the discus as far as I can. Now, it can be 60, it can be 65, it can be 70 metres. Whether I get the medal or not, that's another story. I just want to do my best."

— Seema Kaliramna

Rudra, now four, will again watch from home. Before the CWG, Kaliramna had spoken about how difficult it was to leave him behind. She returned with a medal then, and hopes to do the same from Japan. She also dreams that one day the roles will reverse — that Rudra will be the one competing, and she and Monu will be the ones traveling with him.

For now, the Asian Games are the next step. "We will climb one more step towards the Olympics after winning a medal at the Asian Games," she said. Given what the last three years have required, one more step seems well within her reach.
